# Canon: the canon checker

How the canon checker behaves now, and why. It is the canon of the package `@bigmistqke/canon`. Its terms and its claims are written in Alloy, and the statement of a claim, or of a term that defines a word, is said from its predicate by `canon generate`, so that the units can be checked against each other. [The canon skill](../../skills/canon/SKILL.md) describes the method.

<!-- toc:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
- [`@term checker`](#term-checker) — Checker is the program the canon describes.
- [`@term unit`](#term-unit) — A unit is an axiom, a fact, a spec, an exception, a bug, a conflict or a term.
- [`@term axiom`](#term-axiom) — An axiom is a unit that states a value: how the project wants the world of the people using it to be.
- [`@term fact`](#term-fact) — A fact is a unit that states how the platform under the project is, whatever the project does.
- [`@term spec`](#term-spec) — A spec is a unit that states what the system does, so that a test could contradict it.
- [`@term exception`](#term-exception) — An exception is a unit that states where a fact keeps a spec from holding fully.
- [`@term bug`](#term-bug) — A bug is a unit that states where the code breaks the spec it sits in.
- [`@term conflict`](#term-conflict) — A conflict is a unit that states where units of the canon cannot all hold, until the owner of the design rules which one does.
- [`@term term`](#term-term) — A term is a unit that states a word of the project's language: what the thing it names is.
- [`@term sit`](#term-sit) — A unit sits in the unit whose heading holds its own heading.
- [`@term derive`](#term-derive) — A unit derives from each unit a link on its "Derives from:" line names.
- [`@term link`](#term-link) — A unit links to each unit a link in its body names.
- [`@term cite`](#term-cite) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit) and every unit_2: unit_1 cites unit_2 exactly when unit_1 [sits in](#term-sit) unit_2 or [derives from](#term-derive) unit_2.
- [`@term finding`](#term-finding) — A finding is a freelancing, a misnesting, an untracking, a mistracking, an outdated tracking, an unpairing, an unpinning, an unexplained failure, an untesting, a rotting, an uncitation, a misaiming, an overreach, an orphaning, a misanchoring, a misindexing, a mislocation or a cycle.
- [`@term freelancing`](#term-freelancing) — A freelancing is a finding for a unit that makes a claim and cites nothing it derives from.
- [`@term misnesting`](#term-misnesting) — A misnesting is a finding for a unit that cites a kind of unit it may not cite.
- [`@term unfounded`](#term-unfounded) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): unit_1 is unfounded exactly when unit_1 is one of these: - a [spec](#term-spec) that [cites](#term-cite) no [axiom](#term-axiom) and cites no spec - an [exception](#term-exception) that cites no spec or cites no [fact](#term-fact) - a [bug](#term-bug) that cites no spec
- [`@term miscited`](#term-miscited) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): unit_1 is miscited exactly when unit_1 is one of these: - an [axiom](#term-axiom) that [cites](#term-cite) a unit that is not an axiom - a [fact](#term-fact) that cites a unit - a [spec](#term-spec) that cites a unit that is not an axiom, a spec or a fact - an [exception](#term-exception) that cites a unit that is not a spec or a fact - a [bug](#term-bug) that cites a unit that is not a spec - a [conflict](#term-conflict) that cites a unit - a [term](#term-term) that cites a unit
- [`@term depend`](#term-depend) — A unit depends on a unit when the unit cites the unit. A unit depends on a unit when the unit cites a unit that depends on the unit.
- [`@term circular`](#term-circular) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): unit_1 is circular exactly when unit_1 [cites](#term-cite) a unit that [depends on](#term-depend) unit_1.
- [`@term cycle`](#term-cycle) — A cycle is a finding for a unit that depends on itself.
- [`@term untracking`](#term-untracking) — An untracking is a finding for a bug or a conflict that names no issue.
- [`@term mistracking`](#term-mistracking) — A mistracking is a finding for a bug or a conflict that names an issue the tracker does not know, or one that is a pull request.
- [`@term outdated-tracking`](#term-outdated-tracking) — An outdated tracking is a finding for a bug or a conflict that names an issue the tracker has closed.
- [`@term unpairing`](#term-unpairing) — An unpairing is a finding for a conflict that sets fewer than two units against each other.
- [`@term unpinning`](#term-unpinning) — An unpinning is a finding for a plain test that checks a bug.
- [`@term unexplained-failure`](#term-unexplained-failure) — An unexplained failure is a finding for an expected failure that checks no bug and no exception.
- [`@term untesting`](#term-untesting) — An untesting is a finding for a leaf spec, an exception or a bug that no test checks.
- [`@term rotting`](#term-rotting) — A rotting is a finding for a tag that names no unit, names a file as well as a unit, or names an id that two documents declare, and for a pointer that names no target.
- [`@term uncitation`](#term-uncitation) — An uncitation is a finding for a test in a declared suite that carries no tag.
- [`@term misaiming`](#term-misaiming) — A misaiming is a finding for a test in a declared suite that checks a unit that is no claim.
- [`@term overreach`](#term-overreach) — An overreach is a finding for a test that checks a claim another claim refines.
- [`@term orphaning`](#term-orphaning) — An orphaning is a finding for a unit that nothing uses.
- [`@term misanchoring`](#term-misanchoring) — A misanchoring is a finding for a unit whose heading holds a word after its id, so the anchor the page renders is not the id a pointer names.
- [`@term misindexing`](#term-misindexing) — A misindexing is a finding for a document with no index, or with an index that does not match it.
- [`@term mislocation`](#term-mislocation) — A mislocation is a finding for a claim that names a site no source holds.
- [`@term claim`](#term-claim) — A claim is a spec, an exception or a bug.
- [`@term refined`](#term-refined) — For every [claim_1](#term-claim): claim_1 is refined exactly when a [spec](#term-spec) [sits in](#term-sit) claim_1 or an [exception](#term-exception) sits in claim_1.
- [`@term unguarded`](#term-unguarded) — For every [claim_1](#term-claim): claim_1 is unguarded exactly when claim_1 is not [refined](#term-refined) and is not [tested](#term-tested).
- [`@term adrift`](#term-adrift) — For every [test_1](#term-test): test_1 is adrift exactly when at least one of these holds: - [project](#term-project) [declares](#term-declare) test_1 and test_1 [carries](#term-carry) no [tag](#term-tag) - project declares test_1 and test_1 [checks](#term-check) a [unit](#term-unit) that is not a [claim](#term-claim) - test_1 checks a claim that is [refined](#term-refined)
- [`@term test`](#term-test) — A test is a plain test or an expected failure.
- [`@term project`](#term-project) — Project is the package whose canon field names the canon.
- [`@term declare`](#term-declare) — Project declares each test in each suite that the canon field of the project names.
- [`@term pointer`](#term-pointer) — A pointer is a file pointer or a fragment pointer.
- [`@term file-pointer`](#term-file-pointer) — A file pointer is a pointer with no fragment: it names a [file](#term-file).
- [`@term fragment-pointer`](#term-fragment-pointer) — A fragment pointer is a pointer with a fragment, after a `#`: it names the unit or the [section](#term-section) whose id the fragment holds, in the file its path names.
- [`@term target`](#term-target) — A target is a unit, a section or a file.
- [`@term section`](#term-section) — A section is an element with an id that names no unit.
- [`@term file`](#term-file) — A file is a file of the project.
- [`@term used`](#term-used) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): unit_1 is used exactly when another unit [sits in](#term-sit) unit_1, a [pointer](#term-pointer) [names](#term-name) unit_1 or a [tag](#term-tag) names unit_1.
- [`@term trailer`](#term-trailer) — A trailer is a word that follows the id in the heading of a unit.
- [`@term repeat`](#term-repeat) — A unit repeats what spells the id of the unit in a heading of another unit.
- [`@term follow`](#term-follow) — A trailer follows the unit whose heading holds the trailer.
- [`@term document`](#term-document) — A document is a file that the canon field of the project names.
- [`@term index`](#term-index) — An index is the generated table of contents of a document.
- [`@term hold`](#term-hold) — A document holds each unit and each index in the document. A source holds each symbol that its code declares.
- [`@term match`](#term-match) — An index matches the document that generate writes the index for.
- [`@term site`](#term-site) — A site is a symbol in a source, as the site line of a claim writes it.
- [`@term source`](#term-source) — A source is a module in the sources that the canon field of the project names.
- [`@term code-span`](#term-code-span) — A code span is text between backticks in a document.
- [`@term comment`](#term-comment) — A comment is a comment in a source.
- [`@term tag`](#term-tag) — A tag is a line of the documentation comment of a test.
- [`@term carry`](#term-carry) — A test carries each tag in the documentation comment of the test.
- [`@term plain-test`](#term-plain-test) — A plain test is a test that passes when what it checks holds.
- [`@term expected-failure`](#term-expected-failure) — An expected failure is a test that is marked to fail, with `it.fails` or `test.fails`: it fails until the defect it checks is fixed.
- [`@term check`](#term-check) — For every [test_1](#term-test) and every [unit_1](#term-unit): test_1 checks unit_1 exactly when test_1 [carries](#term-carry) a [tag](#term-tag) that [names](#term-name) unit_1.
- [`@term issue`](#term-issue) — An issue is an entry of the tracker of the project.
- [`@term tracker`](#term-tracker) — Tracker is the issue tracker the scope of the project names.
- [`@term name`](#term-name) — A bug names each issue that the issue line of the bug names.
- [`@term tested`](#term-tested) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): unit_1 is tested exactly when at least one of these holds: - a [test](#term-test) [checks](#term-check) unit_1 - unit_1 is a [spec](#term-spec) and a test checks a [bug](#term-bug) that [sits in](#term-sit) unit_1
- [`@term paired`](#term-paired) — For every [conflict_1](#term-conflict): conflict_1 is paired exactly when conflict_1 [names](#term-name) a [unit](#term-unit) and names another unit.
- [`@term hidden`](#term-hidden) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): unit_1 is hidden exactly when unit_1 is one of these: - a [bug](#term-bug) that [names](#term-name) no [issue](#term-issue), names an issue that [tracker](#term-tracker) does not know, names an issue that tracker has closed or is not [tested](#term-tested) - a [conflict](#term-conflict) that names no issue, names an issue that tracker does not know, names an issue that tracker has closed or is not [paired](#term-paired)
- [`@term misleading`](#term-misleading) — For every [test_1](#term-test): test_1 is misleading exactly when test_1 is one of these: - an [expected failure](#term-expected-failure) that [checks](#term-check) no [bug](#term-bug) and checks no [exception](#term-exception) - a [plain test](#term-plain-test) that checks a bug
- [`@term plugin`](#term-plugin) — A plugin is a package that adds commands to the checker, and that a document asks for by the name of the package.
- [`@term command`](#term-command) — A command is a word after `canon` on the command line, and asks the checker for one job.
- [`@term frontmatter`](#term-frontmatter) — A frontmatter is the block between two lines of three dashes at the top of a document, which names the plugins the document asks for.
- [`@term entry`](#term-entry) — An entry is one string of the list of plugins in a frontmatter.
- [`@term list`](#term-list) — For every [frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter) and every [plugin_1](#term-plugin): frontmatter_1 lists plugin_1 exactly when frontmatter_1 holds an [entry](#term-entry) that spells plugin_1.
- [`@term flaw`](#term-flaw) — A flaw is a mistake that makes a frontmatter unreadable.
- [`@term apply`](#term-apply) — For every [plugin_1](#term-plugin) and every [document_1](#term-document): plugin_1 applies to document_1 exactly when at least one of these holds: - plugin_1 is a plugin inside the package of the [checker](#term-checker) and document_1 starts with no [listing frontmatter](#term-frontmatter) - document_1 starts with a listing frontmatter that [lists](#term-list) plugin_1
- [`@term run`](#term-run) — A run is one call of the checker on the command line, with a command and the documents it names.
- [`@term call`](#term-call) — For every [run_1](#term-run) and every [plugin_1](#term-plugin): run_1 calls plugin_1 exactly when all of these hold: - run_1 asks for a [command](#term-command) that plugin_1 adds - plugin_1 is a plugin inside the package of the [checker](#term-checker) or [applies](#term-apply) to a [document](#term-document)
- [`@term availability`](#term-availability) — For every [command_1](#term-command): command_1 is available exactly when at least one of these holds: - command_1 is a command that the [checker](#term-checker) has of its own - an [inside plugin](#term-plugin) adds command_1 - there are installed_plugin_1 and [document_1](#term-document) such that installed_plugin_1 [applies](#term-apply) to document_1 and adds command_1
- [`@term statement`](#term-statement) — A statement is the quote under the heading of a unit that says in words what the unit claims.
- [`@term word`](#term-word) — A word is a signature, a field of a signature or a predicate that a document declares in its model, and that its readings say.
- [`@axiom every-claim-says-what-it-follows-from`](#axiom-every-claim-says-what-it-follows-from) — All of these hold: - for every [unit_1](#term-unit): when unit_1 is [unfounded](#term-unfounded), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [finding](#term-finding) for unit_1 - for every unit_1: when unit_1 is [miscited](#term-miscited), checker reports a finding for unit_1 - for every unit_1: when unit_1 is [circular](#term-circular), checker reports a finding for unit_1.
  - [`@spec an-unfounded-unit-is-freelancing`](#spec-an-unfounded-unit-is-freelancing) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when unit_1 is [unfounded](#term-unfounded), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [freelancing](#term-freelancing) for unit_1.
    - [`@spec a-spec-cites-an-axiom-or-a-spec`](#spec-a-spec-cites-an-axiom-or-a-spec) — For every [spec_1](#term-spec): when spec_1 [cites](#term-cite) no [axiom](#term-axiom) and cites no spec, [checker](#term-checker) reports a [freelancing](#term-freelancing) for spec_1.
    - [`@spec an-exception-cites-a-spec`](#spec-an-exception-cites-a-spec) — For every [exception_1](#term-exception): when exception_1 [cites](#term-cite) no [spec](#term-spec), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [freelancing](#term-freelancing) for exception_1.
    - [`@spec an-exception-cites-a-fact`](#spec-an-exception-cites-a-fact) — For every [exception_1](#term-exception): when exception_1 [cites](#term-cite) no [fact](#term-fact), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [freelancing](#term-freelancing) for exception_1.
    - [`@spec a-bug-cites-a-spec`](#spec-a-bug-cites-a-spec) — For every [bug_1](#term-bug): when bug_1 [cites](#term-cite) no [spec](#term-spec), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [freelancing](#term-freelancing) for bug_1.
    - [`@bug a-link-in-the-body-counts-as-a-citation`](#bug-a-link-in-the-body-counts-as-a-citation) — When a spec links to an axiom, and the spec cites no axiom, and the spec cites no spec, checker reports no freelancing for the spec.
  - [`@spec a-miscited-unit-is-misnested`](#spec-a-miscited-unit-is-misnested) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when unit_1 is [miscited](#term-miscited), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misnesting](#term-misnesting) for unit_1.
    - [`@spec an-axiom-cites-only-axioms`](#spec-an-axiom-cites-only-axioms) — For every [axiom_1](#term-axiom): when axiom_1 [cites](#term-cite) a [unit](#term-unit) that is not an axiom, [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misnesting](#term-misnesting) for axiom_1.
    - [`@spec a-fact-cites-nothing`](#spec-a-fact-cites-nothing) — For every [fact_1](#term-fact): when fact_1 [cites](#term-cite) a [unit](#term-unit), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misnesting](#term-misnesting) for fact_1.
    - [`@spec a-spec-cites-only-axioms-specs-and-facts`](#spec-a-spec-cites-only-axioms-specs-and-facts) — For every [spec_1](#term-spec): when spec_1 [cites](#term-cite) a [unit](#term-unit) that is not an [axiom](#term-axiom), a spec or a [fact](#term-fact), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misnesting](#term-misnesting) for spec_1.
    - [`@spec an-exception-cites-only-specs-and-facts`](#spec-an-exception-cites-only-specs-and-facts) — For every [exception_1](#term-exception): when exception_1 [cites](#term-cite) a [unit](#term-unit) that is not a [spec](#term-spec) or a [fact](#term-fact), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misnesting](#term-misnesting) for exception_1.
    - [`@spec a-bug-cites-only-specs`](#spec-a-bug-cites-only-specs) — For every [bug_1](#term-bug): when bug_1 [cites](#term-cite) a [unit](#term-unit) that is not a [spec](#term-spec), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misnesting](#term-misnesting) for bug_1.
    - [`@spec a-conflict-cites-nothing`](#spec-a-conflict-cites-nothing) — For every [conflict_1](#term-conflict): when conflict_1 [cites](#term-cite) a [unit](#term-unit), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misnesting](#term-misnesting) for conflict_1.
    - [`@spec a-term-cites-nothing`](#spec-a-term-cites-nothing) — For every [term_1](#term-term): when term_1 [cites](#term-cite) a [unit](#term-unit), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misnesting](#term-misnesting) for term_1.
    - [`@bug a-derives-from-line-is-not-checked-for-its-kind`](#bug-a-derives-from-line-is-not-checked-for-its-kind) — When a fact derives from a unit, and the fact sits in no unit, checker reports no misnesting for the fact.
  - [`@spec a-unit-does-not-depend-on-itself`](#spec-a-unit-does-not-depend-on-itself) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when unit_1 is [circular](#term-circular), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [cycle](#term-cycle) for unit_1.
- [`@axiom a-known-defect-stays-in-sight`](#axiom-a-known-defect-stays-in-sight) — All of these hold: - for every [bug_1](#term-bug): when bug_1 is [hidden](#term-hidden), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [finding](#term-finding) for bug_1 - for every [conflict_1](#term-conflict): when conflict_1 is hidden, checker reports a finding for conflict_1 - for every [test_1](#term-test): when test_1 is [misleading](#term-misleading), checker reports a finding for test_1.
  - [`@spec a-hidden-bug-is-reported`](#spec-a-hidden-bug-is-reported) — For every [bug_1](#term-bug): when bug_1 is [hidden](#term-hidden), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [finding](#term-finding) for bug_1.
    - [`@spec a-bug-names-an-issue`](#spec-a-bug-names-an-issue) — For every [bug_1](#term-bug): when bug_1 [names](#term-name) no [issue](#term-issue), [checker](#term-checker) reports an [untracking](#term-untracking) for bug_1.
    - [`@spec a-bug-names-an-issue-the-tracker-knows`](#spec-a-bug-names-an-issue-the-tracker-knows) — For every [bug_1](#term-bug): when bug_1 [names](#term-name) an [issue](#term-issue) that [tracker](#term-tracker) does not know, [checker](#term-checker) reports a [mistracking](#term-mistracking) for bug_1.
    - [`@spec a-bug-names-an-open-issue`](#spec-a-bug-names-an-open-issue) — For every [bug_1](#term-bug): when bug_1 [names](#term-name) an [issue](#term-issue) that [tracker](#term-tracker) has closed, [checker](#term-checker) reports an [outdated tracking](#term-outdated-tracking) for bug_1.
    - [`@spec a-bug-is-tested`](#spec-a-bug-is-tested) — For every [bug_1](#term-bug): when bug_1 is not [tested](#term-tested), [checker](#term-checker) reports an [untesting](#term-untesting) for bug_1.
  - [`@spec a-hidden-conflict-is-reported`](#spec-a-hidden-conflict-is-reported) — For every [conflict_1](#term-conflict): when conflict_1 is [hidden](#term-hidden), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [finding](#term-finding) for conflict_1.
    - [`@spec a-conflict-names-an-issue`](#spec-a-conflict-names-an-issue) — For every [conflict_1](#term-conflict): when conflict_1 [names](#term-name) no [issue](#term-issue), [checker](#term-checker) reports an [untracking](#term-untracking) for conflict_1.
    - [`@spec a-conflict-names-an-issue-the-tracker-knows`](#spec-a-conflict-names-an-issue-the-tracker-knows) — For every [conflict_1](#term-conflict): when conflict_1 [names](#term-name) an [issue](#term-issue) that [tracker](#term-tracker) does not know, [checker](#term-checker) reports a [mistracking](#term-mistracking) for conflict_1.
    - [`@spec a-conflict-names-an-open-issue`](#spec-a-conflict-names-an-open-issue) — For every [conflict_1](#term-conflict): when conflict_1 [names](#term-name) an [issue](#term-issue) that [tracker](#term-tracker) has closed, [checker](#term-checker) reports an [outdated tracking](#term-outdated-tracking) for conflict_1.
    - [`@spec a-conflict-names-two-units`](#spec-a-conflict-names-two-units) — For every [conflict_1](#term-conflict): when conflict_1 is not [paired](#term-paired), [checker](#term-checker) reports an [unpairing](#term-unpairing) for conflict_1.
  - [`@spec a-misleading-test-is-reported`](#spec-a-misleading-test-is-reported) — For every [test_1](#term-test): when test_1 is [misleading](#term-misleading), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [finding](#term-finding) for test_1.
    - [`@spec an-expected-failure-checks-a-bug-or-an-exception`](#spec-an-expected-failure-checks-a-bug-or-an-exception) — For every [expected_failure_1](#term-expected-failure): when expected_failure_1 [checks](#term-check) no [bug](#term-bug) and checks no [exception](#term-exception), [checker](#term-checker) reports an [unexplained failure](#term-unexplained-failure) for expected_failure_1.
    - [`@spec a-plain-test-does-not-check-a-bug`](#spec-a-plain-test-does-not-check-a-bug) — For every [plain_test_1](#term-plain-test): when plain_test_1 [checks](#term-check) a [bug](#term-bug), [checker](#term-checker) reports an [unpinning](#term-unpinning) for plain_test_1.
- [`@axiom a-canon-cannot-go-out-of-date-unnoticed`](#axiom-a-canon-cannot-go-out-of-date-unnoticed) — All of these hold: - for every [claim_1](#term-claim): when claim_1 is [unguarded](#term-unguarded), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [finding](#term-finding) for claim_1 - for every [tag_1](#term-tag): when tag_1 [names](#term-name) no [unit](#term-unit), checker reports a finding for tag_1 - for every [test_1](#term-test): when test_1 is [adrift](#term-adrift), checker reports a finding for test_1 - for every [pointer_1](#term-pointer): when pointer_1 names no [target](#term-target), checker reports a finding for pointer_1 - for every unit_1: when unit_1 is not [used](#term-used) and is not a [conflict](#term-conflict), checker reports a finding for unit_1 - for every unit_1: when a [trailer](#term-trailer) [follows](#term-follow) unit_1, checker reports a finding for unit_1 - for every [document_1](#term-document): when document_1 [holds](#term-hold) a unit and holds no [index](#term-index), checker reports a finding for document_1 - for every document_1: when document_1 holds an index that does not [match](#term-match) document_1, checker reports a finding for document_1 - for every claim_1: when claim_1 names a [site](#term-site) that no [source](#term-source) holds, checker reports a finding for claim_1 - for every unit_1: when unit_1 [repeats](#term-repeat) a unit, checker reports a finding for unit_1.
  - [`@spec an-unguarded-claim-is-untested`](#spec-an-unguarded-claim-is-untested) — For every [claim_1](#term-claim): when claim_1 is [unguarded](#term-unguarded), [checker](#term-checker) reports an [untesting](#term-untesting) for claim_1.
  - [`@spec a-tag-names-a-unit`](#spec-a-tag-names-a-unit) — For every [tag_1](#term-tag): when tag_1 [names](#term-name) no [unit](#term-unit), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [rotting](#term-rotting) for tag_1.
  - [`@spec an-adrift-test-is-reported`](#spec-an-adrift-test-is-reported) — For every [test_1](#term-test): when test_1 is [adrift](#term-adrift), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [finding](#term-finding) for test_1.
    - [`@spec a-declared-test-carries-a-tag`](#spec-a-declared-test-carries-a-tag) — For every [test_1](#term-test): when [project](#term-project) [declares](#term-declare) test_1 and test_1 [carries](#term-carry) no [tag](#term-tag), [checker](#term-checker) reports an [uncitation](#term-uncitation) for test_1.
    - [`@spec a-declared-test-checks-only-claims`](#spec-a-declared-test-checks-only-claims) — For every [test_1](#term-test): when [project](#term-project) [declares](#term-declare) test_1 and test_1 [checks](#term-check) a [unit](#term-unit) that is not a [claim](#term-claim), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misaiming](#term-misaiming) for test_1.
    - [`@spec a-test-checks-only-leaves`](#spec-a-test-checks-only-leaves) — For every [test_1](#term-test): when test_1 [checks](#term-check) a [claim](#term-claim) that is [refined](#term-refined), [checker](#term-checker) reports an [overreach](#term-overreach) for test_1.
  - [`@spec a-pointer-names-a-target`](#spec-a-pointer-names-a-target) — For every [pointer_1](#term-pointer): when pointer_1 [names](#term-name) no [target](#term-target), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [rotting](#term-rotting) for pointer_1.
    - [`@bug a-file-pointer-is-not-checked`](#bug-a-file-pointer-is-not-checked) — When a file pointer names no target, checker reports no rotting for the file pointer.
  - [`@spec a-unit-is-declared-once`](#spec-a-unit-is-declared-once) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when unit_1 [repeats](#term-repeat) a unit, [checker](#term-checker) reports a [rotting](#term-rotting) for unit_1.
    - [`@bug a-unit-repeated-in-one-document-is-not-reported`](#bug-a-unit-repeated-in-one-document-is-not-reported) — When a document holds a unit, and the document holds another unit that the unit repeats, checker reports no rotting for the unit.
  - [`@spec a-unit-is-used`](#spec-a-unit-is-used) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when unit_1 is not [used](#term-used) and is not a [conflict](#term-conflict), [checker](#term-checker) reports an [orphaning](#term-orphaning) for unit_1.
    - [`@bug a-link-in-a-code-span-uses-a-unit`](#bug-a-link-in-a-code-span-uses-a-unit) — When a unit is not used, and a code span names the unit, checker reports no orphaning for the unit.
  - [`@spec a-heading-ends-with-its-id`](#spec-a-heading-ends-with-its-id) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when a [trailer](#term-trailer) [follows](#term-follow) unit_1, [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misanchoring](#term-misanchoring) for unit_1.
  - [`@spec a-document-holds-an-index`](#spec-a-document-holds-an-index) — For every [document_1](#term-document): when document_1 [holds](#term-hold) a [unit](#term-unit) and holds no [index](#term-index), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misindexing](#term-misindexing) for document_1.
  - [`@spec an-index-matches-its-document`](#spec-an-index-matches-its-document) — For every [document_1](#term-document): when document_1 [holds](#term-hold) an [index](#term-index) that does not [match](#term-match) document_1, [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misindexing](#term-misindexing) for document_1.
  - [`@spec a-site-is-held-by-a-source`](#spec-a-site-is-held-by-a-source) — For every [claim_1](#term-claim): when claim_1 [names](#term-name) a [site](#term-site) that no [source](#term-source) [holds](#term-hold), [checker](#term-checker) reports a [mislocation](#term-mislocation) for claim_1.
    - [`@bug a-site-named-in-a-comment-is-held`](#bug-a-site-named-in-a-comment-is-held) — When a claim names a site that no source holds, and a comment names the site, checker reports no mislocation for the claim.
- [`@axiom a-check-the-project-asked-for-is-never-dropped-silently`](#axiom-a-check-the-project-asked-for-is-never-dropped-silently) — For every [run_1](#term-run): when at least one of these holds: - there are [frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter) and [missing_plugin_1](#term-plugin) such that frontmatter_1 [lists](#term-list) missing_plugin_1 - there is a [document_1](#term-document) such that [checker](#term-checker) reports that document_1 has a frontmatter it cannot read - run_1 asks for a [command](#term-command) that is not [available](#term-availability) - run_1 gets code 2 from a plugin then run_1 exits with code 2.
  - [`@spec a-document-gets-the-plugins-it-asks-for`](#spec-a-document-gets-the-plugins-it-asks-for) — For every [plugin_1](#term-plugin) and every [document_1](#term-document): all of these hold: - when plugin_1 [applies](#term-apply) to document_1, [checker](#term-checker) runs plugin_1 over document_1 - when the command line of a [run](#term-run) does not name document_1 and checker runs plugin_1 over document_1, plugin_1 applies to document_1
    - [`@spec a-document-with-no-plugins-list-gets-the-plugins-inside-the-package`](#spec-a-document-with-no-plugins-list-gets-the-plugins-inside-the-package) — For every [inside_plugin_1](#term-plugin) and every [document_1](#term-document): when document_1 starts with no [listing frontmatter](#term-frontmatter), [checker](#term-checker) runs inside_plugin_1 over document_1.
    - [`@spec a-plugin-a-document-lists-runs-over-it`](#spec-a-plugin-a-document-lists-runs-over-it) — For every [plugin_1](#term-plugin) and every [document_1](#term-document) and every [listing_frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter): when document_1 starts with listing_frontmatter_1 and listing_frontmatter_1 [lists](#term-list) plugin_1, [checker](#term-checker) runs plugin_1 over document_1.
    - [`@spec a-plugin-a-document-does-not-list-does-not-run-over-it`](#spec-a-plugin-a-document-does-not-list-does-not-run-over-it) — For every [plugin_1](#term-plugin) and every [document_1](#term-document) and every [listing_frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter): when all of these hold: - document_1 starts with listing_frontmatter_1 - listing_frontmatter_1 does not [list](#term-list) plugin_1 - the command line of a [run](#term-run) does not name document_1 then [checker](#term-checker) does not run plugin_1 over document_1.
    - [`@spec an-empty-list-asks-for-no-plugin`](#spec-an-empty-list-asks-for-no-plugin) — For every [plugin_1](#term-plugin) and every [document_1](#term-document) and every [listing_frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter): when all of these hold: - document_1 starts with listing_frontmatter_1 - listing_frontmatter_1 holds no [entry](#term-entry) - the command line of a [run](#term-run) does not name document_1 then [checker](#term-checker) does not run plugin_1 over document_1.
    - [`@spec a-document-named-on-the-command-line-is-checked-whatever-its-frontmatter-says`](#spec-a-document-named-on-the-command-line-is-checked-whatever-its-frontmatter-says) — For every [run_1](#term-run) and every [plugin_1](#term-plugin) and every given_document_1: when run_1 [calls](#term-call) plugin_1, [checker](#term-checker) runs plugin_1 over given_document_1.
  - [`@spec a-frontmatter-lists-what-is-written-in-it`](#spec-a-frontmatter-lists-what-is-written-in-it) — For every [frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter) and every [entry_1](#term-entry): when frontmatter_1 holds entry_1, then all of these hold: - frontmatter_1 is a frontmatter with a plugins key - frontmatter_1 has entry_1 between its brackets or has entry_1 after a dash
    - [`@spec an-inline-list-holds-the-entries-between-its-brackets`](#spec-an-inline-list-holds-the-entries-between-its-brackets) — For every [inline_frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter) and every [entry_1](#term-entry): when inline_frontmatter_1 has entry_1 between its brackets, inline_frontmatter_1 holds entry_1.
    - [`@spec a-dashed-list-holds-the-entries-after-its-dashes`](#spec-a-dashed-list-holds-the-entries-after-its-dashes) — For every [dashed_frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter) and every [entry_1](#term-entry): when dashed_frontmatter_1 has entry_1 after a dash, dashed_frontmatter_1 holds entry_1.
    - [`@spec a-comma-inside-quotes-ends-no-entry`](#spec-a-comma-inside-quotes-ends-no-entry) — For every [entry_1](#term-entry) and every quoted_comma_1: entry_1 does not end at quoted_comma_1.
    - [`@spec a-frontmatter-with-no-plugins-key-holds-no-entry`](#spec-a-frontmatter-with-no-plugins-key-holds-no-entry) — For every [frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter): when frontmatter_1 is not a frontmatter with a plugins key, frontmatter_1 holds no [entry](#term-entry).
  - [`@spec only-a-block-at-the-top-is-a-frontmatter`](#spec-only-a-block-at-the-top-is-a-frontmatter) — For every [block_1](#term-frontmatter): when block_1 is a frontmatter, block_1 is a block that starts its [document](#term-document).
  - [`@spec a-flawed-frontmatter-is-refused`](#spec-a-flawed-frontmatter-is-refused) — For every [frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter): when at least one of these holds: - frontmatter_1 has the [flaw](#term-flaw) of an entry that starts with an at sign outside quotes - frontmatter_1 has the flaw of a key that the [checker](#term-checker) does not know - frontmatter_1 has the flaw of a list that is not closed - frontmatter_1 has the flaw of a string that is not closed - frontmatter_1 has the flaw of a key that appears twice then frontmatter_1 is a frontmatter that the checker cannot read.
    - [`@spec a-misquoted-entry-is-refused`](#spec-a-misquoted-entry-is-refused) — For every [misquoted_frontmatter_1](#term-flaw): misquoted_frontmatter_1 is a [frontmatter](#term-frontmatter) that the [checker](#term-checker) cannot read.
    - [`@spec the-refusal-of-a-misquoted-entry-says-to-write-it-in-quotes`](#spec-the-refusal-of-a-misquoted-entry-says-to-write-it-in-quotes) — For every [misquoted_frontmatter_1](#term-flaw): [checker](#term-checker) tells the author to write the name in quotes for misquoted_frontmatter_1.
    - [`@spec a-key-the-checker-does-not-know-is-refused`](#spec-a-key-the-checker-does-not-know-is-refused) — For every [foreign_frontmatter_1](#term-flaw): foreign_frontmatter_1 is a [frontmatter](#term-frontmatter) that the [checker](#term-checker) cannot read.
    - [`@spec a-list-that-is-not-closed-is-refused`](#spec-a-list-that-is-not-closed-is-refused) — For every [unclosed_frontmatter_1](#term-flaw): unclosed_frontmatter_1 is a [frontmatter](#term-frontmatter) that the [checker](#term-checker) cannot read.
    - [`@spec a-string-that-is-not-closed-is-refused`](#spec-a-string-that-is-not-closed-is-refused) — For every [unterminated_frontmatter_1](#term-flaw): unterminated_frontmatter_1 is a [frontmatter](#term-frontmatter) that the [checker](#term-checker) cannot read.
    - [`@spec a-key-written-twice-is-refused`](#spec-a-key-written-twice-is-refused) — For every [doubled_frontmatter_1](#term-flaw): doubled_frontmatter_1 is a [frontmatter](#term-frontmatter) that the [checker](#term-checker) cannot read.
  - [`@spec a-refused-frontmatter-fails-the-run`](#spec-a-refused-frontmatter-fails-the-run) — For every [run_1](#term-run) and every [document_1](#term-document) and every [refused_frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter): when document_1 starts with refused_frontmatter_1, [checker](#term-checker) reports that document_1 has a frontmatter it cannot read and run_1 exits with code 2.
    - [`@spec a-document-with-a-refused-frontmatter-is-reported`](#spec-a-document-with-a-refused-frontmatter-is-reported) — For every [document_1](#term-document) and every [refused_frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter): when document_1 starts with refused_frontmatter_1, [checker](#term-checker) reports that document_1 has a frontmatter it cannot read.
    - [`@spec a-report-of-an-unreadable-frontmatter-stops-the-run`](#spec-a-report-of-an-unreadable-frontmatter-stops-the-run) — For every [run_1](#term-run): when there is a [document_1](#term-document) such that [checker](#term-checker) reports that document_1 has a [frontmatter](#term-frontmatter) it cannot read, run_1 exits with code 2.
  - [`@spec a-plugin-the-project-lacks-fails-the-run`](#spec-a-plugin-the-project-lacks-fails-the-run) — For every [run_1](#term-run) and every [frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter) and every [missing_plugin_1](#term-plugin): when frontmatter_1 [lists](#term-list) missing_plugin_1, [checker](#term-checker) reports that the project lacks missing_plugin_1 and run_1 exits with code 2.
    - [`@spec a-missing-plugin-is-reported`](#spec-a-missing-plugin-is-reported) — For every [frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter) and every [missing_plugin_1](#term-plugin): when frontmatter_1 [lists](#term-list) missing_plugin_1, [checker](#term-checker) reports that the project lacks missing_plugin_1.
    - [`@spec a-missing-plugin-stops-the-run`](#spec-a-missing-plugin-stops-the-run) — For every [run_1](#term-run) and every [frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter) and every [missing_plugin_1](#term-plugin): when frontmatter_1 [lists](#term-list) missing_plugin_1, run_1 exits with code 2.
    - [`@spec the-report-of-a-missing-plugin-offers-the-plugins-inside`](#spec-the-report-of-a-missing-plugin-offers-the-plugins-inside) — For every [plugin_1](#term-plugin) and every inside_plugin_1: when [checker](#term-checker) reports that the project lacks plugin_1, checker offers inside_plugin_1 in place of plugin_1.
  - [`@spec an-unknown-command-fails-the-run`](#spec-an-unknown-command-fails-the-run) — For every [run_1](#term-run) and every [command_1](#term-command): when run_1 asks for command_1 and command_1 is not [available](#term-availability), [checker](#term-checker) reports command_1 as an unknown command and run_1 exits with code 2.
    - [`@spec a-command-that-is-not-available-is-reported-as-unknown`](#spec-a-command-that-is-not-available-is-reported-as-unknown) — For every [run_1](#term-run) and every [command_1](#term-command): when run_1 asks for command_1 and command_1 is not [available](#term-availability), [checker](#term-checker) reports command_1 as an unknown command.
    - [`@spec a-command-that-is-not-available-stops-the-run`](#spec-a-command-that-is-not-available-stops-the-run) — For every [run_1](#term-run) and every [command_1](#term-command): when run_1 asks for command_1 and command_1 is not [available](#term-availability), run_1 exits with code 2.
    - [`@spec an-available-command-is-not-reported-as-unknown`](#spec-an-available-command-is-not-reported-as-unknown) — For every [command_1](#term-command): when command_1 is [available](#term-availability), [checker](#term-checker) does not report command_1 as an unknown command.
  - [`@spec every-plugin-a-run-calls-runs`](#spec-every-plugin-a-run-calls-runs) — For every [run_1](#term-run) and every [plugin_1](#term-plugin): when run_1 [calls](#term-call) plugin_1, run_1 gets code 0 from plugin_1, gets code 1 from plugin_1 or gets code 2 from plugin_1.
  - [`@spec a-run-exits-with-the-worst-code-of-its-plugins`](#spec-a-run-exits-with-the-worst-code-of-its-plugins) — For every [run_1](#term-run): all of these hold: - when run_1 gets code 2 from a [plugin](#term-plugin), run_1 exits with code 2 - when run_1 gets code 1 from a plugin and gets code 2 from no plugin, run_1 exits with code 1
    - [`@spec a-plugin-that-could-not-run-stops-the-run`](#spec-a-plugin-that-could-not-run-stops-the-run) — For every [run_1](#term-run): when run_1 gets code 2 from a [plugin](#term-plugin), run_1 exits with code 2.
    - [`@spec a-finding-fails-the-run`](#spec-a-finding-fails-the-run) — For every [run_1](#term-run): when run_1 gets code 1 from a [plugin](#term-plugin) and gets code 2 from no plugin, run_1 exits with code 1.
    - [`@spec a-run-with-no-finding-succeeds`](#spec-a-run-with-no-finding-succeeds) — For every [run_1](#term-run): when there is no [plugin_1](#term-plugin) such that run_1 gets code 1 from plugin_1 or gets code 2 from plugin_1, run_1 exits with code 0.
  - [`@spec a-frontmatter-changes-nothing-but-the-plugins-of-its-document`](#spec-a-frontmatter-changes-nothing-but-the-plugins-of-its-document) — For every [document_1](#term-document) and every document_2: when document_1 is document_2 without its [frontmatter](#term-frontmatter), then all of these hold: - for every [unit_1](#term-unit): all of these hold: - when document_2 [holds](#term-hold) unit_1, document_1 holds unit_1 - when document_1 holds unit_1, document_2 holds unit_1 - when [checker](#term-checker) reports a [finding](#term-finding) for document_2, checker reports a finding for document_1 - when checker reports a finding for document_1, checker reports a finding for document_2
    - [`@spec a-frontmatter-leaves-the-units-of-its-document-as-they-were`](#spec-a-frontmatter-leaves-the-units-of-its-document-as-they-were) — For every [document_1](#term-document) and every document_2: when document_1 is document_2 without its [frontmatter](#term-frontmatter), then for every [unit_1](#term-unit): all of these hold: - when document_2 [holds](#term-hold) unit_1, document_1 holds unit_1 - when document_1 holds unit_1, document_2 holds unit_1
    - [`@spec a-frontmatter-changes-no-finding`](#spec-a-frontmatter-changes-no-finding) — For every [document_1](#term-document) and every document_2: when document_1 is document_2 without its [frontmatter](#term-frontmatter), then all of these hold: - when [checker](#term-checker) reports a [finding](#term-finding) for document_2, checker reports a finding for document_1 - when checker reports a finding for document_1, checker reports a finding for document_2
    - [`@spec generate-keeps-the-frontmatter-of-a-document`](#spec-generate-keeps-the-frontmatter-of-a-document) — For every [document_1](#term-document) and every document_2: when [checker](#term-checker) generates document_2 from document_1, then for every [frontmatter_1](#term-frontmatter): all of these hold: - when document_1 starts with frontmatter_1, document_2 starts with frontmatter_1 - when document_2 starts with frontmatter_1, document_1 starts with frontmatter_1
- [`@axiom a-statement-says-what-its-logic-says`](#axiom-a-statement-says-what-its-logic-says) — For every [document_1](#term-document) and every [unit_1](#term-unit): when all of these hold: - document_1 keeps readings - document_1 [holds](#term-hold) unit_1 - unit_1 holds a formula - the [statement](#term-statement) of unit_1 is not current then [checker](#term-checker) reports the statement of unit_1.
  - [`@spec a-document-that-keeps-no-readings-is-left-as-it-is`](#spec-a-document-that-keeps-no-readings-is-left-as-it-is) — For every [document_1](#term-document) and every [unit_1](#term-unit): when document_1 [holds](#term-hold) unit_1 and keeps no readings, then all of these hold: - [checker](#term-checker) does not write the [statement](#term-statement) of unit_1 when it generates - checker does not report the statement of unit_1
  - [`@spec a-document-that-does-not-name-the-plugin-is-left-as-it-is`](#spec-a-document-that-does-not-name-the-plugin-is-left-as-it-is) — For every [alloy_plugin_1](#term-plugin) and every [document_1](#term-document) and every [unit_1](#term-unit): when [checker](#term-checker) does not run alloy_plugin_1 over document_1 and document_1 [holds](#term-hold) unit_1, then all of these hold: - checker does not write the [statement](#term-statement) of unit_1 when it generates - checker does not report the statement of unit_1
  - [`@spec a-unit-with-a-formula-and-no-statement-is-unwritten`](#spec-a-unit-with-a-formula-and-no-statement-is-unwritten) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when unit_1 holds a formula, has no [statement](#term-statement) and the formula of unit_1 can be said in words, the statement of unit_1 is unwritten.
  - [`@spec a-generated-statement-that-differs-from-its-formula-is-stale`](#spec-a-generated-statement-that-differs-from-its-formula-is-stale) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when all of these hold: - unit_1 holds a formula - the [statement](#term-statement) of unit_1 sits between the markers of a generated region - the statement of unit_1 differs from what its formula says - the formula of unit_1 can be said in words then the statement of unit_1 is stale.
  - [`@spec a-generated-statement-that-its-formula-would-say-again-is-current`](#spec-a-generated-statement-that-its-formula-would-say-again-is-current) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when all of these hold: - the [statement](#term-statement) of unit_1 sits between the markers of a generated region - the statement of unit_1 does not differ from what its formula says - the formula of unit_1 can be said in words then the statement of unit_1 is current.
  - [`@spec a-statement-that-a-person-wrote-is-handwritten`](#spec-a-statement-that-a-person-wrote-is-handwritten) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when all of these hold: - unit_1 holds a formula - unit_1 has a [statement](#term-statement) - the statement of unit_1 does not sit between the markers of a generated region - the formula of unit_1 can be said in words then the statement of unit_1 is handwritten.
  - [`@spec a-formula-that-the-readings-cannot-say-is-unsayable`](#spec-a-formula-that-the-readings-cannot-say-is-unsayable) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when the formula of unit_1 names a word that has no reading or unit_1 holds more than one formula, the formula of unit_1 cannot be said in words.
    - [`@spec a-formula-with-a-word-that-has-no-reading-is-unsayable`](#spec-a-formula-with-a-word-that-has-no-reading-is-unsayable) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when the formula of unit_1 names a word that has no reading, the formula of unit_1 cannot be said in words.
    - [`@spec a-unit-with-two-formulas-is-unsayable`](#spec-a-unit-with-two-formulas-is-unsayable) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when unit_1 holds more than one formula, the formula of unit_1 cannot be said in words.
    - [`@spec the-report-of-an-unsayable-formula-says-why`](#spec-the-report-of-an-unsayable-formula-says-why) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when the formula of unit_1 cannot be said in words, [checker](#term-checker) says why the formula of unit_1 cannot be said.
  - [`@spec generate-writes-what-is-not-current-and-nothing-else`](#spec-generate-writes-what-is-not-current-and-nothing-else) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): all of these hold: - when [checker](#term-checker) writes the [statement](#term-statement) of unit_1 when it generates, the statement of unit_1 is unwritten or the statement of unit_1 is stale - when the statement of unit_1 is unwritten or the statement of unit_1 is stale, checker writes the statement of unit_1 when it generates
    - [`@spec generate-writes-the-statement-of-an-unwritten-unit-between-markers`](#spec-generate-writes-the-statement-of-an-unwritten-unit-between-markers) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when the [statement](#term-statement) of unit_1 is unwritten, then all of these hold: - [checker](#term-checker) writes the statement of unit_1 when it generates - checker writes the statement of unit_1 between markers, just below its heading
    - [`@spec generate-writes-the-statement-of-a-stale-unit-again`](#spec-generate-writes-the-statement-of-a-stale-unit-again) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when the [statement](#term-statement) of unit_1 is stale, [checker](#term-checker) writes the statement of unit_1 when it generates.
    - [`@spec generate-writes-a-statement-as-a-quote-that-markdown-reads-as-paragraphs-and-lists`](#spec-generate-writes-a-statement-as-a-quote-that-markdown-reads-as-paragraphs-and-lists) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when [checker](#term-checker) writes the [statement](#term-statement) of unit_1 when it generates, checker writes the statement of unit_1 as a quote that Markdown reads as paragraphs and lists.
    - [`@spec generate-leaves-a-current-statement-as-it-is`](#spec-generate-leaves-a-current-statement-as-it-is) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when the [statement](#term-statement) of unit_1 is current, [checker](#term-checker) does not write the statement of unit_1 when it generates.
    - [`@spec generate-never-overwrites-a-handwritten-statement`](#spec-generate-never-overwrites-a-handwritten-statement) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when the [statement](#term-statement) of unit_1 is handwritten, [checker](#term-checker) does not write the statement of unit_1 when it generates.
    - [`@spec generate-leaves-an-unsayable-unit-as-it-is`](#spec-generate-leaves-an-unsayable-unit-as-it-is) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when the formula of unit_1 cannot be said in words, [checker](#term-checker) does not write the [statement](#term-statement) of unit_1 when it generates.
  - [`@spec check-reports-a-statement-that-is-not-current`](#spec-check-reports-a-statement-that-is-not-current) — For every [document_1](#term-document) and every [unit_1](#term-unit): when all of these hold: - document_1 keeps readings - document_1 [holds](#term-hold) unit_1 - unit_1 holds a formula - the [statement](#term-statement) of unit_1 is not current then [checker](#term-checker) reports the statement of unit_1.
  - [`@spec check-does-not-report-a-current-statement`](#spec-check-does-not-report-a-current-statement) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when the [statement](#term-statement) of unit_1 is current, [checker](#term-checker) does not report the statement of unit_1.
  - [`@spec a-report-of-a-statement-fails-check`](#spec-a-report-of-a-statement-fails-check) — For every [run_1](#term-run) and every [check_command_1](#term-command) and every [unit_1](#term-unit): when run_1 asks for check_command_1 and [checker](#term-checker) reports the [statement](#term-statement) of unit_1, run_1 does not exit with code 0.
  - [`@spec generate-fails-on-a-handwritten-statement-and-says-so`](#spec-generate-fails-on-a-handwritten-statement-and-says-so) — For every [run_1](#term-run) and every [generate_command_1](#term-command) and every [unit_1](#term-unit): when run_1 asks for generate_command_1 and the [statement](#term-statement) of unit_1 is handwritten, [checker](#term-checker) reports the statement of unit_1 and run_1 does not exit with code 0.
  - [`@spec generate-fails-on-an-unsayable-formula-and-says-why`](#spec-generate-fails-on-an-unsayable-formula-and-says-why) — For every [run_1](#term-run) and every [generate_command_1](#term-command) and every [unit_1](#term-unit): when run_1 asks for generate_command_1 and the formula of unit_1 cannot be said in words, [checker](#term-checker) says why the formula of unit_1 cannot be said and run_1 does not exit with code 0.
  - [`@spec the-prose-check-does-not-read-a-generated-statement`](#spec-the-prose-check-does-not-read-a-generated-statement) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit): when the [statement](#term-statement) of unit_1 sits between the markers of a generated region, the prose check does not read the statement of unit_1.
  - [`@spec a-word-that-a-reading-says-and-nothing-declares-is-undeclared`](#spec-a-word-that-a-reading-says-and-nothing-declares-is-undeclared) — For every [word_1](#term-word): when all of these hold: - there is a [unit_1](#term-unit) such that a reading in unit_1 says word_1 - no unit declares word_1 then word_1 is a word that a reading says and nothing declares.
  - [`@spec a-word-declared-outside-a-term-is-misplaced`](#spec-a-word-declared-outside-a-term-is-misplaced) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit) and every [word_1](#term-word): when unit_1 declares word_1 and is not a [term](#term-term), word_1 is a word declared in a unit that is not a term.
  - [`@spec a-reading-apart-from-the-declaration-it-says-is-apart`](#spec-a-reading-apart-from-the-declaration-it-says-is-apart) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit) and every [word_1](#term-word): when a reading in unit_1 says word_1, a unit declares word_1 and unit_1 does not declare word_1, word_1 is a word whose reading is in another unit than its declaration.
  - [`@spec a-declared-word-that-no-claim-uses-is-unused`](#spec-a-declared-word-that-no-claim-uses-is-unused) — For every [word_1](#term-word): when all of these hold: - a [unit](#term-unit) declares word_1 - there is no unit_1 such that a claim, a definition or a fact of unit_1 uses word_1 then word_1 is a word that no claim, definition or fact uses.
  - [`@spec a-word-that-a-fact-a-parent-signature-or-a-predicate-names-is-used`](#spec-a-word-that-a-fact-a-parent-signature-or-a-predicate-names-is-used) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit) and every [word_1](#term-word): when a fact, a parent signature or a predicate in unit_1 names word_1, there is a unit_2 such that a claim, a definition or a fact of unit_2 uses word_1.
  - [`@spec a-field-that-another-signature-shares-is-used-only-through-its-own-signature`](#spec-a-field-that-another-signature-shares-is-used-only-through-its-own-signature) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit) and every [word_1](#term-word): when all of these hold: - word_1 is a field whose name another signature gives to a field too - a claim, a definition or a fact of unit_1 uses word_1 then unit_1 uses word_1 through its own signature.
  - [`@spec a-word-declared-in-a-term-said-beside-it-and-used-is-not-reported`](#spec-a-word-declared-in-a-term-said-beside-it-and-used-is-not-reported) — For every [term_1](#term-term) and every [word_1](#term-word): when all of these hold: - term_1 declares word_1 - a reading in term_1 says word_1 - there is a [unit_1](#term-unit) such that a claim, a definition or a fact of unit_1 uses word_1 then all of these hold: - word_1 is not a word that a reading says and nothing declares - word_1 is not a word declared in a unit that is not a term - word_1 is not a word whose reading is in another unit than its declaration - word_1 is not a word that no claim, definition or fact uses - [checker](#term-checker) does not report the word word_1
  - [`@spec a-document-that-keeps-no-readings-has-no-word-reported`](#spec-a-document-that-keeps-no-readings-has-no-word-reported) — For every [document_1](#term-document) and every [unit_1](#term-unit) and every [word_1](#term-word): when document_1 keeps no readings, [holds](#term-hold) unit_1 and unit_1 declares word_1, then all of these hold: - word_1 is not a word that a reading says and nothing declares - word_1 is not a word declared in a unit that is not a term - word_1 is not a word whose reading is in another unit than its declaration - word_1 is not a word that no claim, definition or fact uses - [checker](#term-checker) does not report the word word_1
  - [`@spec a-signature-a-field-and-a-predicate-are-declared-words`](#spec-a-signature-a-field-and-a-predicate-are-declared-words) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit) and every [word_1](#term-word): when a model block of unit_1 writes the declaration of word_1, unit_1 declares word_1.
  - [`@spec a-declaration-in-a-comment-declares-nothing`](#spec-a-declaration-in-a-comment-declares-nothing) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit) and every [word_1](#term-word): when only a comment in unit_1 writes the declaration of word_1, unit_1 does not declare word_1.
  - [`@spec a-reading-is-keyed-by-a-field-alone-or-with-its-signature-or-as-a-primed-set`](#spec-a-reading-is-keyed-by-a-field-alone-or-with-its-signature-or-as-a-primed-set) — For every [unit_1](#term-unit) and every [word_1](#term-word): when a reading in unit_1 is keyed to word_1 by the field alone, with its signature, or as a primed set, a reading in unit_1 says word_1.
  - [`@spec a-flagged-word-fails-check`](#spec-a-flagged-word-fails-check) — For every [run_1](#term-run) and every [check_command_1](#term-command) and every [word_1](#term-word): when run_1 asks for check_command_1 and [checker](#term-checker) reports the word word_1, run_1 does not exit with code 0.
  - [`@spec check-reports-nothing-about-a-word-that-is-in-order`](#spec-check-reports-nothing-about-a-word-that-is-in-order) — For every [word_1](#term-word): when all of these hold: - word_1 is not a word that a reading says and nothing declares - word_1 is not a word declared in a unit that is not a term - word_1 is not a word whose reading is in another unit than its declaration - word_1 is not a word that no claim, definition or fact uses then [checker](#term-checker) does not report the word word_1.
  - [`@spec check-reports-a-word-that-is-not-in-order`](#spec-check-reports-a-word-that-is-not-in-order) — For every [word_1](#term-word): when at least one of these holds: - word_1 is a word that a reading says and nothing declares - word_1 is a word declared in a unit that is not a term - word_1 is a word whose reading is in another unit than its declaration - word_1 is a word that no claim, definition or fact uses then [checker](#term-checker) reports the word word_1.
<!-- toc:end -->

## Terms

### @term checker

> Checker is the program the canon describes.

The program `canon`, with its commands `check`, `generate`, `tree`, `lint`, `logic` and `log`, and the commands that its [plugins](#term-plugin) add. A canon holds [units](#term-unit).

```alloy bounds
for 6
```

A canon the checker finds nothing wrong with must exist: an axiom, a spec that sits in it, a test that is declared and carries a tag that names the spec, and a document that holds both with an index that matches it.

```alloy scenario
some a: Axiom, s: Spec, t: Test, g: Tag, d: Document, i: Index | s->a in Sit.rel and t in Declared and t->g in Carry.rel and g->s in Name.tag and d->a in Hold.units and d->s in Hold.units and d->i in Hold.indexes and i->d in Match.rel and no Finding
```

A bug that is kept in sight must exist: it names an issue the tracker knows and has not closed, and an expected failure checks it.

```alloy scenario
some b: Bug, x: ExpectedFailure, i: Issue | b->i in Name.issue and i in Known and i not in Closed and checks[x, b] and b not in Finding and x not in Finding
```

A conflict that is kept in sight must exist: it names an open issue and sets two units against each other.

```alloy scenario
some c: Conflict, i: Issue, u, v: Unit | u != v and c->i in Name.issue and i in Known and i not in Closed and c->u in Name.between and c->v in Name.between and c not in Finding
```

### @term unit

> A unit is an axiom, a fact, a spec, an exception, a bug, a conflict or a term.

One entry of a canon: a heading with a kind and a stem, and a statement under it. A unit is an [axiom](#term-axiom), a [fact](#term-fact), a [spec](#term-spec), an [exception](#term-exception), a [bug](#term-bug), a [conflict](#term-conflict) or a [term](#term-term).

```alloy vocabulary
abstract sig Unit extends Thing {}
```

```readings
noun Unit: [unit]
Unit: {1} is a [unit] | {1} is not a [unit]
```

### @term axiom

> An axiom is a unit that states a value: how the project wants the world of the people using it to be.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Axiom extends Unit {}
```

```readings
noun Axiom: [axiom]
Axiom: {1} is an [axiom] | {1} is not an [axiom]
```

### @term fact

> A fact is a unit that states how the platform under the project is, whatever the project does.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Fact extends Unit {}
```

```readings
noun Fact: [fact]
Fact: {1} is a [fact] | {1} is not a [fact]
```

### @term spec

> A spec is a unit that states what the system does, so that a test could contradict it.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Spec extends Claim {}
```

```readings
noun Spec: [spec]
Spec: {1} is a [spec] | {1} is not a [spec]
```

### @term exception

> An exception is a unit that states where a fact keeps a spec from holding fully.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Exception extends Claim {}
```

```readings
noun Exception: [exception]
Exception: {1} is an [exception] | {1} is not an [exception]
```

### @term bug

> A bug is a unit that states where the code breaks the spec it sits in.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Bug extends Claim {}
```

```readings
noun Bug: [bug]
Bug: {1} is a [bug] | {1} is not a [bug]
```

### @term conflict

> A conflict is a unit that states where units of the canon cannot all hold, until the owner of the design rules which one does.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Conflict extends Unit {}
```

```readings
noun Conflict: [conflict]
Conflict: {1} is a [conflict] | {1} is not a [conflict]
```

### @term term

> A term is a unit that states a word of the project's language: what the thing it names is.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Term extends Unit {}
```

```readings
noun Term: [term]
Term: {1} is a [term] | {1} is not a [term]
```

### @term sit

> A unit sits in the unit whose heading holds its own heading.

A unit sitting in another is nested there.

```alloy vocabulary
one sig Sit { rel: Unit -> Unit }
```

```readings
Sit.rel: {1} [sits in] {2} | {1} does not [sit in] {2}
```

### @term derive

> A unit derives from each unit a link on its "Derives from:" line names.

That line comes right after the unit's statement.

```alloy vocabulary
one sig Derive { rel: Unit -> Unit }
```

```readings
Derive.rel: {1} [derives from] {2} | {1} does not [derive from] {2}
```

### @term link

> A unit links to each unit a link in its body names.

A link elsewhere than the "Derives from:" line is a reference: it cites nothing.

### @term cite

<!-- statement-term-cite:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [unit_1](#term-unit) and every unit_2:
>
> unit_1 cites unit_2 exactly when unit_1 [sits in](#term-sit) unit_2 or [derives from](#term-derive) unit_2.
<!-- statement-term-cite:end -->

Nesting and the "Derives from:" line are the two ways a unit says what it follows from. A unit [sits in](#term-sit) or [derives from](#term-derive) what it cites. A [link](#term-link) in the body is neither.

```alloy
pred cites[u, v: Unit] { u->v in Sit.rel or u->v in Derive.rel }
```

```readings
cites: {1} [cites] {2} | {1} does not [cite] {2}
```

### @term finding

> A finding is a freelancing, a misnesting, an untracking, a mistracking, an outdated tracking, an unpairing, an unpinning, an unexplained failure, an untesting, a rotting, an uncitation, a misaiming, an overreach, an orphaning, a misanchoring, a misindexing, a mislocation or a cycle.

What `check` reports on a unit, a test or a link. The canon gives each finding a noun of its own, and its term says what the [checker](#term-checker) prints for it.

```alloy vocabulary
abstract sig Thing {}
sig Finding in Thing {}
fact finding_kinds { Finding = Freelancing + Misnesting + Untracking + Mistracking + OutdatedTracking + Unpairing + Unpinning + UnexplainedFailure + Untesting + Rotting + Uncitation + Misaiming + Overreach + Orphaning + Misanchoring + Misindexing + Mislocation + Cycle }
```

```readings
Finding: [checker](#term-checker) reports a [finding] for {1} | [checker](#term-checker) reports no [finding] for {1}
```

### @term freelancing

> A freelancing is a finding for a unit that makes a claim and cites nothing it derives from.

The checker prints `freelancing`.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Freelancing in Finding {}
```

```readings
Freelancing: [checker](#term-checker) reports a [freelancing] for {1} | [checker](#term-checker) reports no [freelancing] for {1}
```

### @term misnesting

> A misnesting is a finding for a unit that cites a kind of unit it may not cite.

The checker prints `misnested`.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Misnesting in Finding {}
```

```readings
Misnesting: [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misnesting] for {1} | [checker](#term-checker) reports no [misnesting] for {1}
```

### @term unfounded

<!-- statement-term-unfounded:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [unit_1](#term-unit):
>
> unit_1 is unfounded exactly when unit_1 is one of these:
> - a [spec](#term-spec) that [cites](#term-cite) no [axiom](#term-axiom) and cites no spec
> - an [exception](#term-exception) that cites no spec or cites no [fact](#term-fact)
> - a [bug](#term-bug) that cites no spec
<!-- statement-term-unfounded:end -->

A unit that lacks a citation its kind owes: what it follows from.

```alloy
pred unfounded[u: Unit] {
  (u in Spec and (no a: Axiom | cites[u, a]) and (no s: Spec | cites[u, s]))
  or (u in Exception and (no s: Spec | cites[u, s]))
  or (u in Exception and (no f: Fact | cites[u, f]))
  or (u in Bug and (no s: Spec | cites[u, s]))
}
```

```readings
unfounded: {1} is [unfounded] | {1} is not [unfounded]
```

### @term miscited

<!-- statement-term-miscited:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [unit_1](#term-unit):
>
> unit_1 is miscited exactly when unit_1 is one of these:
> - an [axiom](#term-axiom) that [cites](#term-cite) a unit that is not an axiom
> - a [fact](#term-fact) that cites a unit
> - a [spec](#term-spec) that cites a unit that is not an axiom, a spec or a fact
> - an [exception](#term-exception) that cites a unit that is not a spec or a fact
> - a [bug](#term-bug) that cites a unit that is not a spec
> - a [conflict](#term-conflict) that cites a unit
> - a [term](#term-term) that cites a unit
<!-- statement-term-miscited:end -->

A unit that cites a kind of unit it may not cite. A conflict names the units it sets against each other on a line of its own, which is no citation.

```alloy
pred miscited[u: Unit] {
  (u in Axiom and (some v: Unit | cites[u, v] and v not in Axiom))
  or (u in Fact and (some v: Unit | cites[u, v]))
  or (u in Spec and (some v: Unit | cites[u, v] and v not in Axiom and v not in Spec and v not in Fact))
  or (u in Exception and (some v: Unit | cites[u, v] and v not in Spec and v not in Fact))
  or (u in Bug and (some v: Unit | cites[u, v] and v not in Spec))
  or (u in Conflict and (some v: Unit | cites[u, v]))
  or (u in Term and (some v: Unit | cites[u, v]))
}
```

```readings
miscited: {1} is [miscited] | {1} is not [miscited]
```

### @term depend

> A unit depends on a unit when the unit cites the unit. A unit depends on a unit when the unit cites a unit that depends on the unit.

A unit depends on each unit it follows from: what it cites, what those cite, and so on up. A unit can depend on itself: it follows from itself when it cites itself, or when what it cites leads back to it.

```alloy vocabulary
one sig Depend { rel: Unit -> Unit }
fact depend_closure { Depend.rel = ^(Sit.rel + Derive.rel) }
```

```readings
Depend.rel: {1} [depends on] {2} | {1} does not [depend on] {2}
```

### @term circular

<!-- statement-term-circular:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [unit_1](#term-unit):
>
> unit_1 is circular exactly when unit_1 [cites](#term-cite) a unit that [depends on](#term-depend) unit_1.
<!-- statement-term-circular:end -->

A unit that follows from itself: it cites a unit that [depends](#term-depend) on it, and that unit may be the unit itself. A unit that cites itself is a loop of one, and a unit whose citations lead back to it is a longer loop.

```alloy
pred circular[u: Unit] { some v: Unit | cites[u, v] and v->u in Depend.rel }
```

```readings
circular: {1} is [circular] | {1} is not [circular]
```

### @term cycle

> A cycle is a finding for a unit that depends on itself.

The checker prints `cycle`, once for each loop, with every unit in it.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Cycle in Finding {}
```

```readings
Cycle: [checker](#term-checker) reports a [cycle] for {1} | [checker](#term-checker) reports no [cycle] for {1}
```

### @term untracking

> An untracking is a finding for a bug or a conflict that names no issue.

The checker prints `untracked-bug` or `untracked-conflict`.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Untracking in Finding {}
```

```readings
Untracking: [checker](#term-checker) reports an [untracking] for {1} | [checker](#term-checker) reports no [untracking] for {1}
```

### @term mistracking

> A mistracking is a finding for a bug or a conflict that names an issue the tracker does not know, or one that is a pull request.

The checker prints `missing-issue`.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Mistracking in Finding {}
```

```readings
Mistracking: [checker](#term-checker) reports a [mistracking] for {1} | [checker](#term-checker) reports no [mistracking] for {1}
```

### @term outdated-tracking

> An outdated tracking is a finding for a bug or a conflict that names an issue the tracker has closed.

The checker prints `closed-issue`.

```alloy vocabulary
sig OutdatedTracking in Finding {}
```

```readings
OutdatedTracking: [checker](#term-checker) reports an [outdated tracking] for {1} | [checker](#term-checker) reports no [outdated tracking] for {1}
```

### @term unpairing

> An unpairing is a finding for a conflict that sets fewer than two units against each other.

The checker prints `lone-conflict`.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Unpairing in Finding {}
```

```readings
Unpairing: [checker](#term-checker) reports an [unpairing] for {1} | [checker](#term-checker) reports no [unpairing] for {1}
```

### @term unpinning

> An unpinning is a finding for a plain test that checks a bug.

The checker prints `unpinned-bug`.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Unpinning in Finding {}
```

```readings
Unpinning: [checker](#term-checker) reports an [unpinning] for {1} | [checker](#term-checker) reports no [unpinning] for {1}
```

### @term unexplained-failure

> An unexplained failure is a finding for an expected failure that checks no bug and no exception.

The checker prints `fails-without-bug`.

```alloy vocabulary
sig UnexplainedFailure in Finding {}
```

```readings
UnexplainedFailure: [checker](#term-checker) reports an [unexplained failure] for {1} | [checker](#term-checker) reports no [unexplained failure] for {1}
```

### @term untesting

> An untesting is a finding for a leaf spec, an exception or a bug that no test checks.

The checker prints `untested`.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Untesting in Finding {}
```

```readings
Untesting: [checker](#term-checker) reports an [untesting] for {1} | [checker](#term-checker) reports no [untesting] for {1}
```

### @term rotting

> A rotting is a finding for a tag that names no unit, names a file as well as a unit, or names an id that two documents declare, and for a pointer that names no target.

The checker prints `rot`.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Rotting in Finding {}
```

```readings
Rotting: [checker](#term-checker) reports a [rotting] for {1} | [checker](#term-checker) reports no [rotting] for {1}
```

### @term uncitation

> An uncitation is a finding for a test in a declared suite that carries no tag.

The checker prints `uncited`.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Uncitation in Finding {}
```

```readings
Uncitation: [checker](#term-checker) reports an [uncitation] for {1} | [checker](#term-checker) reports no [uncitation] for {1}
```

### @term misaiming

> A misaiming is a finding for a test in a declared suite that checks a unit that is no claim.

The checker prints `missing-spec`.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Misaiming in Finding {}
```

```readings
Misaiming: [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misaiming] for {1} | [checker](#term-checker) reports no [misaiming] for {1}
```

### @term overreach

> An overreach is a finding for a test that checks a claim another claim refines.

The checker prints `parent-cited`.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Overreach in Finding {}
```

```readings
Overreach: [checker](#term-checker) reports an [overreach] for {1} | [checker](#term-checker) reports no [overreach] for {1}
```

### @term orphaning

> An orphaning is a finding for a unit that nothing uses.

The checker prints `dead`.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Orphaning in Finding {}
```

```readings
Orphaning: [checker](#term-checker) reports an [orphaning] for {1} | [checker](#term-checker) reports no [orphaning] for {1}
```

### @term misanchoring

> A misanchoring is a finding for a unit whose heading holds a word after its id, so the anchor the page renders is not the id a pointer names.

The checker prints `unreachable`.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Misanchoring in Finding {}
```

```readings
Misanchoring: [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misanchoring] for {1} | [checker](#term-checker) reports no [misanchoring] for {1}
```

### @term misindexing

> A misindexing is a finding for a document with no index, or with an index that does not match it.

The checker prints `stale-toc`.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Misindexing in Finding {}
```

```readings
Misindexing: [checker](#term-checker) reports a [misindexing] for {1} | [checker](#term-checker) reports no [misindexing] for {1}
```

### @term mislocation

> A mislocation is a finding for a claim that names a site no source holds.

The checker prints `stale-site`.

```alloy vocabulary
sig Mislocation in Finding {}
```

```readings
Mislocation: [checker](#term-checker) reports a [mislocation] for {1} | [checker](#term-checker) reports no [mislocation] for {1}
```

### @term claim

> A claim is a spec, an exception or a bug.

A unit that a test can contradict.

```alloy vocabulary
abstract sig Claim extends Unit {}
```

```readings
noun Claim: [claim]
Claim: {1} is a [claim] | {1} is not a [claim]
```

### @term refined

<!-- statement-term-refined:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [claim_1](#term-claim):
>
> claim_1 is refined exactly when a [spec](#term-spec) [sits in](#term-sit) claim_1 or an [exception](#term-exception) sits in claim_1.
<!-- statement-term-refined:end -->

A bug that sits in a spec marks where the code breaks the spec. It refines nothing, so a spec that holds only bugs is a leaf.

```alloy
pred refined[c: Claim] { (some s: Spec | s->c in Sit.rel) or (some e: Exception | e->c in Sit.rel) }
```

```readings
refined: {1} is [refined] | {1} is not [refined]
```

### @term unguarded

<!-- statement-term-unguarded:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [claim_1](#term-claim):
>
> claim_1 is unguarded exactly when claim_1 is not [refined](#term-refined) and is not [tested](#term-tested).
<!-- statement-term-unguarded:end -->

A leaf that no test checks: the code can stop doing what it says, and no test fails.

```alloy
pred unguarded[c: Claim] { not refined[c] and not tested[c] }
```

```readings
unguarded: {1} is [unguarded] | {1} is not [unguarded]
```

### @term adrift

<!-- statement-term-adrift:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [test_1](#term-test):
>
> test_1 is adrift exactly when at least one of these holds:
> - [project](#term-project) [declares](#term-declare) test_1 and test_1 [carries](#term-carry) no [tag](#term-tag)
> - project declares test_1 and test_1 [checks](#term-check) a [unit](#term-unit) that is not a [claim](#term-claim)
> - test_1 checks a claim that is [refined](#term-refined)
<!-- statement-term-adrift:end -->

A test whose tags do not say which leaf it checks.

```alloy
pred adrift[t: Test] {
  (t in Declared and (no g: Tag | t->g in Carry.rel))
  or (t in Declared and (some u: Unit | checks[t, u] and u not in Claim))
  or (some c: Claim | checks[t, c] and refined[c])
}
```

```readings
adrift: {1} is [adrift] | {1} is not [adrift]
```

### @term name

> A bug names each issue that the issue line of the bug names.

A bug or a conflict names an issue on its "Issue:" line. A conflict names the units it sets against each other on its "Between:" line. A tag names the unit whose id it holds.

A pointer names the target its path and fragment lead to. A claim names the site on its "Site:" line. A comment names each site whose symbol it holds. A code span names each unit whose id the link syntax inside it holds.

```alloy vocabulary
one sig Name {
  issue: (Bug + Conflict) -> Issue,
  between: Conflict -> Unit,
  tag: Tag -> Unit,
  pointer: Pointer -> Target,
  site: Claim -> Site
}
```

```readings
Name.tag: {1} [names] {2} | {1} does not [name] {2}
```

### @term tested

<!-- statement-term-tested:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [unit_1](#term-unit):
>
> unit_1 is tested exactly when at least one of these holds:
> - a [test](#term-test) [checks](#term-check) unit_1
> - unit_1 is a [spec](#term-spec) and a test checks a [bug](#term-bug) that [sits in](#term-sit) unit_1
<!-- statement-term-tested:end -->

A test of a bug asserts what the spec the bug breaks claims, so it tests that spec too. A plain test that checks a bug still makes the bug tested: the checker reports the test instead, as [misleading](#term-misleading).

```alloy
pred tested[u: Unit] {
  (some t: Test | checks[t, u])
  or (u in Spec and (some t: Test, b: Bug | checks[t, b] and b->u in Sit.rel))
}
```

```readings
tested: {1} is [tested] | {1} is not [tested]
```

### @term paired

<!-- statement-term-paired:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [conflict_1](#term-conflict):
>
> conflict_1 is paired exactly when conflict_1 [names](#term-name) a [unit](#term-unit) and names another unit.
<!-- statement-term-paired:end -->

A conflict needs two sides.

```alloy
pred paired[c: Conflict] { some a, b: Unit | a != b and c->a in Name.between and c->b in Name.between }
```

```readings
paired: {1} is [paired] | {1} is not [paired]
```

### @term hidden

<!-- statement-term-hidden:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [unit_1](#term-unit):
>
> unit_1 is hidden exactly when unit_1 is one of these:
> - a [bug](#term-bug) that [names](#term-name) no [issue](#term-issue), names an issue that [tracker](#term-tracker) does not know, names an issue that tracker has closed or is not [tested](#term-tested)
> - a [conflict](#term-conflict) that names no issue, names an issue that tracker does not know, names an issue that tracker has closed or is not [paired](#term-paired)
<!-- statement-term-hidden:end -->

A known defect out of sight: no open issue tracks it, no test checks it, or a conflict that does not say which units it sets against each other.

```alloy
pred hidden[x: Unit] {
  (x in Bug and ((no i: Issue | x->i in Name.issue) or (some i: Issue | x->i in Name.issue and i not in Known) or (some i: Issue | x->i in Name.issue and i in Closed) or not tested[x]))
  or (x in Conflict and ((no i: Issue | x->i in Name.issue) or (some i: Issue | x->i in Name.issue and i not in Known) or (some i: Issue | x->i in Name.issue and i in Closed) or not paired[x]))
}
```

```readings
hidden: {1} is [hidden] | {1} is not [hidden]
```

### @term misleading

<!-- statement-term-misleading:begin — generated by `canon generate`; edits are overwritten -->
> For every [test_1](#term-test):
>
> test_1 is misleading exactly when test_1 is one of these:
> - an [expected failure](#term-expected-failure) that [checks](#term-check) no [bug](#term-bug) and checks no [exception](#term-exception)
> - a [plain test](#term-plain-test) that checks a bug
<!-- statement-term-misleading:end -->

A test whose outcome says nothing true about a defect: an expected failure that names no defect, or a test that passes while the bug it checks is there.

```alloy

  (t in ExpectedFailure and (no b: Bug | checks[t, b]) and (no e: Exception | checks[t, e]))
  or (t in PlainTest and (some b: Bug | checks[t, b]))
}
```

```readings
misleading: {1} is [misleading] | {1} is not [misleading]
```

### @term plugin

> A plugin is a package that adds commands to the checker, and that a document asks for by the name of the package.

```alloy vocabulary
fact plugin_kinds { Plugin = Inside + Installed + Missing and no Inside & Installed and no Inside & Missing and no Installed & Missing }
one sig Offer { rel: Plugin -> Plugin }
```

```readings

noun Installed: [installed plugin]

noun Missing: [missing plugin]
```
